problem: Arnold–Givental conjecture and Arnold conjecture – relating symplectic geometry to Morse theory.
missing_details: Precise definition of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism via a one-parameter family of Hamiltonian functions
Nondegeneracy condition required in the weak form of the Arnold conjecture
Definition of the Morse number as the minimal number of critical points of a Morse function
Specification of which coefficient field is used to compute Betti numbers in the weak conjecture
Definition of a compact Lagrangian submanifold and its characterization as the fixed point locus of an anti-symplectic involution
Definition of an anti-symplectic involution τ satisfying τ*ω=−ω and τ²=id
Transversality condition for φ₁(L) intersecting L in the Arnold–Givental conjecture
Use of ℤ/2ℤ coefficients in the homology bound for the Arnold–Givental conjecture
refined_question: Do the following hold in full generality? (1) Let (M,ω) be a closed symplectic manifold and let H_t:M→ℝ be a smooth family of Hamiltonian functions generating a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ=φ₁:M→M. Is it true that the number of fixed points of φ is at least the minimal number of critical points of any Morse function on M (equivalently, at least ∑_{i=0}^{2n}dim H_i(M;F) for any field F)? (2) Let (M,ω) be a compact 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold and let L⊂M be a compact Lagrangian submanifold arising as the fixed point set of an anti-symplectic involution τ:M→M. For any Hamiltonian isotopy φ_t generated by H_t, if φ₁(L) intersects L transversely, is it true that |φ₁(L)∩L|≥∑_{i=0}^ndim H_i(L;ℤ/2ℤ)?
justification: The original name indicates a relationship between symplectic fixed-point/intersection theory and Morse theoretic bounds, but omits all definitions of the manifolds, maps, and homological invariants involved, as well as the precise inequalities to be proved. The refined question explicitly defines the closed symplectic manifold (M,ω), Hamiltonian diffeomorphism φ via H_t, the compact Lagrangian L fixed by an anti-symplectic involution τ, and the homological lower bounds (Morse number and Betti sum) in exact form, matching the canonical statements in the authoritative source. No further equivalent formulation is stated in the source.
